description: A high temperature (fever) is usually a sign that the body is fighting an infection.

child_flow.question: Does the child have a rash that does not fade when you press a glass against it?
Does the child have a stiff neck, dislike of light, or severe headache?
Is the child very drowsy, difficult to wake, or not responding normally?
Is the child extremely agitated, cannot be comforted, or very confused?
Is the child having breathing problems such as breathing very fast, working hard to breathe, or grunting?
Does the child have unusually cold hands/feet or skin that looks blue, grey, pale or blotchy?
Are there signs of dehydration (very few wet nappies, dry mouth, sunken eyes)?
Is the child refusing to eat or drink, or far less active than usual?
Has the child had a seizure or fit (shaking that does not stop)?
How many days has the fever lasted?
Has the child had similar fevers before?

adult_flow.question: What is your sex assigned at birth?
Are you experiencing unusual nausea, extreme fatigue, or back/jaw pain?
Are you having pain when you pee, or pain in your lower back (kidney area)?
How many days have you had the fever?
Is your fever staying the same or getting worse even after rest or medicine?
Are you having difficulty breathing or breathing very fast?
Are you experiencing chest pain or pressure?
Are you confused, disoriented, or unusually drowsy?
Do you have a stiff neck or pain when bending your neck forward?
Are you shivering uncontrollably or having chills?
Do you have a rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass?
Are you vomiting repeatedly or unable to keep fluids down?
Do you have signs of dehydration (very little urine, very dark urine, dizziness)?
Have you had a seizure at any point?
Are your lips, tongue, or skin blue, grey, or unusually pale?
Have you had similar fevers in the past?
Do you feel extremely unwell or that something is seriously wrong?

risk_factors: Recent surgery, wound, or invasive procedure
Recent travel to areas with serious infectious diseases
Existing heart, lung, kidney, or liver conditions
Feeling very unwell or weak despite treatment
Baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher
Baby 3–6 months with a temperature of 39°C or higher
Long-term medical conditions (heart, lung, kidney, immune problems)
Signs of dehydration (dry mouth, sunken eyes, fewer wet nappies)
Recent contact with someone with a serious infection (meningitis, sepsis, measles)
Parents reporting the child is 'not themselves' or much less responsive
red_flags: Fever not improving or getting worse despite rest, fluids, or over-the-counter medicines
Difficulty breathing or breathing very fast
Chest pain or pressure, especially when breathing or coughing
Confusion, new disorientation, or being hard to wake
Severe stiff neck or a rash that does not fade when pressed with a glass
Blue, grey, or very pale lips or skin
Severe vomiting or signs of dehydration
Seizure or fit
Fever lasting 5 days or longer without improvement
Feeling extremely unwell or feeling that something is seriously wrong
Baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38°C or higher
Baby aged 3–6 months with a temperature of 39°C or higher
Fever in a child lasting 5 days or more
Rash in a child that does not fade when pressed with a glass
Stiff neck, dislike of light, or severe headache in a child
Child who is very drowsy, difficult to wake, or not responding normally
Child who is extremely agitated or very confused
Child breathing very fast, working hard to breathe, grunting, or chest/abdominal retractions
Cold hands and feet or unusual skin colour (blue, grey, very pale, blotchy)
Signs of dehydration in a child (few wet nappies, sunken eyes, dry mouth)
Child not eating or drinking, or much less interested in normal activities
Febrile seizure or shaking that does not stop
safety_disclaimer: This information is for general education only and does not replace a medical assessment.
